title: Symmetric Fabry-Perot Bandpass with Quarter-Wave Bragg Mirrors
scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity structure with quarter-wave Bragg mirrors on both sides can achieve ≥0.95 transmittance at 1550 nm while providing adequate suppression in both 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm stopbands within 30 layers.
design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) alternating high/low index layers create high-reflectance Bragg mirrors. A half-wave cavity layer between two identical mirror stacks produces a narrow transmission peak at the design wavelength. Symmetry ensures balanced stopband performance on both sides of the passband.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses in nm for all 11 layers
cavity layer thickness around λ/2 at 1550 nm
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count is 11 (well under 30 limit)
quarter-wave layers at 1550 nm are approximately 100-150 nm thickness range
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for multilayer thin films
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient stopband depth in both bands simultaneously
Quarter-wave design may be too restrictive for asymmetric stopband requirements
Limited design freedom with fixed periodic structure
execution_request_english: Design a symmetric Fabry-Perot narrowband bandpass filter for 1550 nm LiDAR reception. Incident medium is air. Substrate is Fused Silica. Use only Ta2O5 (Gao) (high index) and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (low index) materials. Stack topology: Air | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao)(cavity) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Ta2O5 (Gao) | SiO2 (Lemarchand) | Fused Silica. This is 11 layers total (5 pairs on each side plus one cavity layer). Optimize all individual layer thicknesses in nanometers. Target wavelength is 1550 nm at normal incidence. Maximize transmittance at 1550 nm with soft target ≥0.95. Minimize transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Total layers must not exceed 30.
